conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, leading to lower expected drawdowns but also limited upside potential.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech and a small amount of leveraged exposure. Expected drawdowns are moderate.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this mode carries substantially higher drawdown risk, and leveraged ETFs are subject to daily decay and rebalancing, which can lead to rapid losses if not managed with strict stop discipline.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to cure the concentration breach and reduce broad index exposure.
Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero, eliminating all leveraged ETFs.
Sell CRWD to zero, cutting high-beta single names.
Trim SMH to 5%, reducing high-beta sector exposure.
Add to QQQI, increasing income exposure to 30% for steady monthly distributions.
This plan prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates heavily into income ETFs and broad index exposure, cutting leverage and high-beta names. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
